questions.q: What are the three parts of a JWT, in order?
o: payload.signature.header
header.payload.signature
signature.payload.header
header.signature.payload
questions.x: A JWT is header.payload.signature. Each part is Base64URL encoded and joined by dots. The signature is computed over the first two parts, so it comes last.
questions.h: The signature covers the other two parts. Which two, and where must the signature sit?

questions.q: What does the JWT signature actually prove?
o: That the token was signed with the key and has not been altered
That the payload is encrypted so only the issuer can read it
That the token expires at a Unix timestamp stored in the header
That the kid field uniquely identifies the subject of the token
questions.x: The signature is created from the encoded header and payload plus a secret, using the algorithm in the header. If either part is changed, the signature no longer matches unless the attacker knows the key.
questions.h: If someone edits the payload, what would fail unless they also know the signing key?

questions.q: Which JWT payload claim is usually the username?
o: iss
exp
sub
kid
questions.x: sub is the subject, usually the username. iss is the issuer. exp is the expiration timestamp. kid is an optional header field that identifies the signing key, not a payload claim.
questions.h: Look at the three common payload claims. Which one names who the token is about?

questions.q: Why can anyone who intercepts a JWT read the payload?
o: The payload is AES-encrypted with a key anyone can recover
The payload is only Base64URL encoded, not encrypted
The signing secret is published in the JWT header kid field
Browsers automatically decrypt JWT payloads sent over HTTPS
questions.x: JWT uses Base64URL encoding so the token is URL-safe. Encoding is not encryption. Anyone with the token can decode the header and payload without the signing key.
questions.h: Base64URL makes the token URL-safe. Does decoding it require the HMAC secret?

questions.q: Which statement about JWT structure is correct?
o: A JWT has three parts joined by dots
The payload can include alg and kid
The header can include iss and sub
All of these statements are true
questions.x: A JWT is header.payload.signature joined by dots. alg and kid belong in the header, not the payload. iss and sub belong in the payload, not the header. All is wrong because those last two claims swap the parts.
questions.h: Which JWT part carries alg and kid, and which part carries iss and sub?
